title: Understanding Codons and Amino Acids
text: Each DNA string is made up of codons, which are sequences of $$3$$ letters. These codons are translated into amino acids. There are $$64$$ possible codons but only $$20$$ amino acids. How can this information help in creating a more compact encoding?

title: Using Amino Acids for Encoding
text: Instead of encoding each letter or codon, consider encoding the amino acids directly. Since there are only $$20$$ amino acids, this can significantly reduce the dimensionality of your data.

title: Calculating Dimensionality
text: If you encode using 3-grams of amino acids, how many possible combinations are there?

title: Dimensionality of 3-grams
text: When using 3-grams of amino acids, the dimensionality is determined by the number of possible combinations of $$3$$ amino acids. Since there are $$20$$ amino acids, the dimensionality is $$20$$.
